Net radiation of the reference surface

Source: R/reference-et.R
ef_ref_net_radiation.Rd

Computes the net radiation \(R_n\) of the hypothetical reference surface (albedo 0.23) and its components, the net shortwave radiation \(R_{ns}\) and the net outgoing longwave radiation \(R_{nl}\), for a daily or an hourly time step and the explicit standard (FAO-56 or the ASCE-EWRI standardized procedure). It is the net radiation entering ef_ref_et() and ef_ref_soil_heat_flux(); it is not the net radiation of a pixel (ef_net_radiation()).

Usage

ef_ref_net_radiation(
  solar_radiation,
  clear_sky_radiation,
  vapour_pressure,
  air_temperature = NULL,
  tmax = NULL,
  tmin = NULL,
  timestep,
  standard,
  cloudiness = NULL
)

Arguments

solar_radiation

Numeric. Measured (or estimated) solar radiation \(R_s\) of the period [MJ m-2 d-1 or MJ m-2 h-1]. Must be finite and >= 0.

clear_sky_radiation

Numeric or NULL. Clear-sky radiation \(R_{so}\) of the same period and unit, from ef_rso(). Must be finite and > 0 where the cloudiness term is computed from \(R_s/R_{so}\). May be NULL only when cloudiness is supplied.

vapour_pressure

Numeric. Actual vapour pressure \(e_a\) [kPa] of the period (from ef_ea_daily() or ef_ea_rh()). Must be finite and >= 0.

air_temperature

Numeric or NULL. Mean hourly air temperature [degrees Celsius], required for timestep = "hourly" (and NULL for "daily"). Must be finite and > -273.16.

tmax, tmin

Numeric or NULL. Daily maximum and minimum air temperatures [degrees Celsius], required for timestep = "daily" (and NULL for "hourly"). Finite, > -273.16 and tmin <= tmax.

timestep

Character, no default. "daily" (FAO-56 Eq. 39; ASCE-EWRI Eq. 17) or "hourly" (FAO-56 chapter 4, "Hourly time step"; ASCE-EWRI Eq. 44).

standard

Character, no default. "fao56" or "asce" (ASCE-EWRI 2005 standardized procedure). It selects the Stefan-Boltzmann constant and the limits of the relative solar radiation (see Details).

cloudiness

Numeric or NULL. The cloudiness term \(f = 1.35 R_s/R_{so} - 0.35\) [-] to use instead of computing it from solar_radiation and clear_sky_radiation, in [-0.35, 1] for "fao56" and in [0.05, 1] for "asce" (the ranges of each standard). It serves night-time (and, for ASCE-EWRI, low sun angle) periods, where the ratio is undefined or unreliable and is carried from an earlier period (see Details). When supplied it is used at every position. Default NULL: computed from the radiation.

Value

An object of class earthflux_reference_net_radiation: a list with

  • rn: net radiation of the reference surface \(R_n\);

  • rns: net shortwave radiation \(R_{ns}\);

  • rnl: net outgoing longwave radiation \(R_{nl}\);

  • cloudiness: the cloudiness term \(f\) used [-];

all numeric [MJ m-2 d-1 or MJ m-2 h-1, the unit of solar_radiation] with the common length (and dim) of the inputs;

  • timestep, standard;

  • flags: list of earthflux_flag records (record scope) for the codes that hold somewhere: EF_INPUT_NA (a required input is missing) and EF_WS_RS_RSO_LIMITED (\(R_s/R_{so}\) outside the range of the standard, limited inside the cloudiness term);

  • provenance: time step, standard, verification status, constants, source of the cloudiness term, references, flags_evaluated and package version.

Details

$$R_{ns} = (1 - \alpha) R_s, \quad \alpha = 0.23$$ (FAO-56, chapter 3, Eq. 38; ASCE-EWRI, 2005, Eqs. 16 and 43: albedo fixed at 0.23 for the short and the tall reference, daily and hourly), $$R_{nl} = \sigma \frac{T_{max,K}^4 + T_{min,K}^4}{2} (0.34 - 0.14 \sqrt{e_a}) \left(1.35 \frac{R_s}{R_{so}} - 0.35\right)$$ with \(T_K = T + 273.16\) (FAO-56, chapter 3, Eq. 39; ASCE-EWRI Eqs. 17-18), and \(R_n = R_{ns} - R_{nl}\) (FAO-56 Eq. 40; ASCE-EWRI Eqs. 15 and 42). For the hourly time step (FAO-56, chapter 4, "Hourly time step"; ASCE-EWRI Eqs. 44-45) the mean of the fourth powers is replaced by \(T_{hr,K}^4\).

Constants and limits of each standard (decision WF-14: the literals of each standard are used as written):

"fao56""asce"
\(\sigma\), daily [MJ K-4 m-2 d-1]4.903e-9 (Eq. 39)4.901e-9 (Eq. 17, p. 19)
\(\sigma\), hourly [MJ K-4 m-2 h-1]4.903e-9 / 242.042e-10 (Eq. 44, p. 34)
\(R_s/R_{so}\) in the cloudiness term\(\le 1\) (Eq. 39)in [0.3, 1] (Eqs. 18 and 45, pp. 20 and 35)
cloudiness term \(f\)[-0.35, 1][0.05, 1] (Eqs. 17 and 44)

The limits act only inside the cloudiness term; solar_radiation and rns are not modified, and the positions where a limit acts are flagged EF_WS_RS_RSO_LIMITED. The report is not consistent here: it states that the ratio limits \(0.3 \le R_s/R_{so} \le 1\) give \(0.05 \le f \le 1\) (pp. 20 and 35), but \(1.35 \times 0.3 - 0.35 = 0.055\). The ratio limit is applied (so a computed term is at least 0.055), and a supplied cloudiness is accepted in the stated range [0.05, 1]. The two Stefan-Boltzmann values differ by 0.04 % (daily); the ASCE-EWRI hourly value is the published one (4.901e-9 / 24 = 2.04208e-10).

Night-time and low sun angle. With \(R_{so} = 0\) the ratio is undefined. FAO-56 sets it to the value of a period 2-3 hours before sunset, identified by \(\omega_s - 0.79 \le \omega \le \omega_s - 0.52\), or, approximately, to 0.4-0.6 in humid and sub-humid and 0.7-0.8 in arid and semi-arid climates (0.3 means complete cloud cover). ASCE-EWRI (2005, Eq. 46, pp. 35-36) uses, for every period whose sun angle at the midpoint is below 0.3 rad (night, dusk and dawn), the cloudiness term of the last period before the sun angle fell below 0.3 rad. Selecting that value is the task of the station orchestration (ef_station_ref_et(), argument night_cloudiness); here the resulting term is passed as cloudiness (for a ratio \(r\), cloudiness = 1.35 * r - 0.35).

Normative constants. \(\sigma\) of each standard (FAO-56 4.903e-9 MJ m-2 d-1 K-4, about 5.6748e-8 W m-2 K-4, 0.08 % below the CODATA value used elsewhere in the package) and 273.16 in the conversion to kelvin, as written in both standards; the package constants (EF_STEFAN_BOLTZMANN, 273.15) are not used inside the reference surface equations. \(R_{nl}\) is an empirical longwave balance of the reference surface and is not interchangeable with the incoming and emitted longwave radiation of a pixel.

Missing values propagate (and are flagged EF_INPUT_NA). Missing, unknown or inconsistent timestep, standard and temperature arguments raise earthflux_missing_input, earthflux_unknown_method or earthflux_input_error; values outside the domains above (including \(R_{so} = 0\) without cloudiness, and tmin > tmax) raise earthflux_domain_error.

Verification status

standard = "fao56": VERIFICADA (FAO-56, chapter 3, Eqs. 38-40; chapter 4, hourly time step; cases V10, V11, V14, V15 and V16 of dev/specs/weather-forcing.md 8.1). standard = "asce": VERIFICADA (ASCE-EWRI, 2005, Eqs. 15-18, pp. 17-20, and Eqs. 42-45, pp. 32-35).

References

Allen, R. G., Pereira, L. S., Raes, D., & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration: Guidelines for computing crop water requirements (FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56). FAO, Rome. ISBN 92-5-104219-5.

ASCE-EWRI (2005). The ASCE Standardized Reference Evapotranspiration Equation. Task Committee on Standardization of Reference Evapotranspiration, Environmental and Water Resources Institute of the American Society of Civil Engineers. Final report, January 2005. Published as Allen, R. G., Walter, I. A., Elliott, R. L., Howell, T. A., Itenfisu, D., Jensen, M. E., & Snyder, R. L. (Eds.), American Society of Civil Engineers, Reston, VA. doi:10.1061/9780784408056

See also

Examples

# FAO-56 example 18 (Uccle, 6 July): daily step
rn <- ef_ref_net_radiation(
  solar_radiation = 22.07, clear_sky_radiation = 30.90,
  vapour_pressure = 1.409, tmax = 21.5, tmin = 12.3, timestep = "daily",
  standard = "fao56"
)
rn$rn
#> [1] 13.28291

# Same inputs with the ASCE-EWRI constants (sigma = 4.901e-9)
ef_ref_net_radiation(
  solar_radiation = 22.07, clear_sky_radiation = 30.90,
  vapour_pressure = 1.409, tmax = 21.5, tmin = 12.3, timestep = "daily",
  standard = "asce"
)$rn
#> [1] 13.28443

# FAO-56 example 19, 02:00-03:00: night, Rs/Rso = 0.8 carried
ef_ref_net_radiation(
  solar_radiation = 0, clear_sky_radiation = NULL,
  vapour_pressure = 3.402, air_temperature = 28, timestep = "hourly",
  standard = "fao56", cloudiness = 1.35 * 0.8 - 0.35
)$rn
#> [1] -0.1003213
